follow-up time: ≤72 hours after birth (for neonatal death outcome)
exposure: Duration of time from initiation of general endotracheal anesthesia (GETA) to delivery
outcome: Composite of complications (continuous positive airway pressure or high-flow nasal cannula for ≥2 consecutive hours, inspired oxygen ≥30% for ≥4 consecutive hours, mechanical ventilation, stillbirth, or neonatal death ≤72 hours after birth)
Composite of maternal morbidity (bladder injury, bowel injury, and extension of hysterotomy)
cohort: 218 patients with singleton nonanomalous gestations undergoing cesarean delivery ≥37 weeks of gestation under GETA with reassuring fetal status
finding: When cesarean delivery is performed at term using GETA without evidence of nonreassuring fetal status prior to delivery, an I-D interval >4 minutes is associated with an increased frequency of perinatal complications.
